tests_run.name: node tools/dodgetest.mjs
tests_run.detail: 6/6 assertions: single tap no dodge, double tap <0.28s dodges, endFrame clears, triple tap not a second dodge, 1s apart no dodge, A-then-D no dodge

issues_found.issue: I-frames do not exist in multiplayer. Damage is shooter-authoritative: _onProjectileHit returns early when item.owner !== this.localId ('the owner reports it') and the shooter emits {type:'hit'}. The new `hittable` filter only removes the LOCAL player from the LOCAL client's target set, so it only blocks bot shots (host-simulated) and self-hits. A human opponent's client has no knowledge of your player.iframes and will happily resolve and report a hit mid-roll. The headline property of the headline feature is single-player-only.
issues_found.suggestion: Make invulnerability authoritative where damage is applied. Either (a) include an `inv` flag in _localReport() and have the sim/room drop 'hit' requests whose target reported inv within the last ~150ms, or (b) validate in the hit handler against the last received remote state. Option (a) is the smaller diff and matches the existing report plumbing.

issues_found.issue: The filtered list is passed to _driveBots(dt, st, hittable), which builds ctx.targets from it. For the 0.12s of i-frames the local player vanishes from every bot's target list entirely — not just from hit resolution but from perception, chase and hide-spot avoidance. Bots may drop aim, re-target, or path away and then snap back, which reads as an AI stutter caused by the victim's dodge.
issues_found.suggestion: Pass the unfiltered `parts` to _driveBots and enforce invulnerability only at the point of damage (the ctx.onHit / onTag callbacks), so bot perception is unchanged.

issues_found.issue: dodge() has no grounded check. Crouching, swimming, frozen and cooldown are all refused, but an airborne player can double-tap into a 14 m/s horizontal air burst that overwrites vel.x/vel.z entirely, ignoring the ACCEL.air/FRICTION.air model. Chained with the 0.8s total lockout this gives a repeatable air-mobility tool that was almost certainly not the design intent for a committed ground roll.
issues_found.suggestion: Add `if (!this.grounded) return false;` to dodge(), or gate air dodges to one per airtime with an explicit reduced speed.

issues_found.issue: Inconsistent i-frame coverage in hide & seek. _hideSeekLocal is called with the unfiltered `parts`, and a bot seeker's tag goes through ctx.onTag using the filtered list — so a bot cannot tag you mid-roll but a human seeker can, and your own tag reach is unaffected. Dodging is a real defensive tech against AI and a no-op against people, in the same mode.
issues_found.suggestion: Decide explicitly whether the roll should dodge tags at all, then apply that rule in one place for both bots and humans (same fix as the HIGH issue).

issues_found.issue: Entering water cancels dodgeTime but leaves dodgeCooldown at its full 0.8s and leaves iframes running. A roll clipped by a puddle costs the full cooldown for a fraction of the distance.
issues_found.suggestion: On the water cancel, also clamp dodgeCooldown down to DODGE.cooldown so the player is not punished for terrain.

issues_found.issue: The dodge pip renders only inside the `h.crosshair && h.alive !== false` branch, so it disappears whenever the crosshair is hidden (e.g. hide-phase / non-combat states) even though the roll is still available. Minor readability gap, not a functional bug.
issues_found.suggestion: Emit the pip alongside the crosshair block rather than nested inside it, if the roll is usable in those states.

verified_correct: Yaw-to-world direction math in _dodgeInput matches the engine convention (forward = (-sin, -cos), right = (cos, -sin)); W/A/S/D and arrow keys map to the correct world directions.
Input.doubleTapped_ is cleared in endFrame() alongside justPressed, so no stale edge signal leaks across frames; the _lastTapAt sentinel (-9) correctly prevents a triple tap becoming two dodges.
reset() clears dodgeTime, dodgeCooldown and iframes, so respawn cannot inherit a live roll.
No new intervals, timers or listeners were added; no memory-leak surface in this diff.
dodgeCharge is clamped 0..1 and the UI re-clamps before rendering; no NaN path found.
untested: Actual game feel — automated QA cannot judge whether 14 m/s / 0.35s / 0.12s i-frames / 0.45s cooldown is fun, readable or overpowered. This needs a human in a match.
Real multiplayer with 2+ human clients; the HIGH issue above was found by reading the netcode path, not by observing a live desync.
Whether the 0.12s i-frame window survives real network latency even after being made authoritative — at 80ms RTT the window is close to a single round trip.
Browser-side rendering: the dodge pip CSS and glow were reviewed as source, not rendered or screenshotted.
Interaction of the roll with terrain collision on the curved planet surface (steep slopes, cliff edges, launching off the world).
Controller/touch input paths, if any exist outside src/core/input.js keyboard handling.
